question: What is the name for the surgical opening of the large intestine onto the belly wall?
explanation: Great job! A stoma is simply the surgically created opening of the bowel onto the tummy surface where waste leaves the body. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T14#GNS212_U1_T14_h1)

question: Why do doctors most commonly perform a colostomy?

options.A: To permanently cure long-term constipation without changing diet
options.B: To bypass or remove a diseased or damaged part of the bowel
options.C: To allow direct medicine administration into the bloodstream
options.D: To increase the length of the small intestine for better food absorption

explanation: Spot on! Conditions like severe infection, injury, or cancer mean we need to safely divert waste away from a sick section of the large intestine. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T14#GNS212_U1_T14_h1)

question: Which type of colostomy usually gives the most firm and solid stool?
explanation: You got it! Because a sigmoid colostomy sits near the very end of the colon, the body has absorbed lots of water, leaving solid stool. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T14#GNS212_U1_T14_h2)

question: What decides how thick or watery a colostomy stool will be?

options.A: The anatomical location of the stoma along the large intestine
options.B: The amount of physical exercise the patient does every day
options.C: The time of day the patient eats their main meal
options.D: The exact brand of the appliance pouch the patient wears

explanation: Exactly! Stool gets thicker the longer it travels through the colon because more water is absorbed along the way. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T14#GNS212_U1_T14_h2)

question: What is the normal, healthy look of a newly made intestinal stoma?
explanation: Correct! A healthy stoma is packed with tiny blood vessels, which gives it a nice moist, pink to brick-red color. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T14#GNS212_U1_T14_h3)

question: During a routine check, what does a pale, dusky, or blue-purple stoma tell you?

options.A: Inadequate blood supply to the stoma tissue
options.C: Too much fluid intake by the patient

explanation: Spot on. Color changes like blue, purple, or paleness mean blood flow is blocked or low—this is a true surgical emergency! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T14#GNS212_U1_T14_h3)

question: Why must the hole on the skin barrier be measured to fit just a tiny bit larger than the stoma?

options.A: To allow for the natural shrinking of the stoma over many years
options.B: To prevent the barrier from rubbing against and injuring the stoma tissue
options.C: To give extra space for air to circulate under the pouch
options.D: To make it easier to empty liquid waste from the bottom

explanation: You nailed it! Cutting the opening slightly larger protects the delicate stoma tissue from painful friction while keeping the skin safe. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T14#GNS212_U1_T14_h4)

question: You are getting ready to put a new colostomy bag on a patient. What is the right first step for the skin?

options.A: Rub a thick layer of oily moisturizing lotion to soften the skin
options.B: Scrub the area hard with an alcohol-based antiseptic
options.C: Dust the moist skin heavily with a scented powder
options.D: Clean the skin gently with warm water and pat it completely dry

explanation: Correct! The skin needs to be clean and totally dry so the adhesive barrier can stick securely without leaking. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T14#GNS212_U1_T14_h4)

question: Which foods are most likely to cause a blockage in a patient with a colostomy?
explanation: Spot on! Foods with tough hulls, skins, or hard fibrous bits don't digest easily and can get stuck right inside the stoma. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T14#GNS212_U1_T14_h5)

question: Which of these foods should a patient expect to cause extra gas and strong odor?
explanation: You got it! Certain sulfur-rich or fermentable foods naturally lead to more tummy gas and stronger stoma smells. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T14#GNS212_U1_T14_h5)

question: What do we call a colostomy problem where the bowel telescopes out and the stoma becomes way too long?
explanation: Correct! A prolapse happens when extra bowel pushes out through the stoma site, making it stick out much further than normal. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T14#GNS212_U1_T14_h6)

question: What is a parastomal hernia in a patient with a colostomy?

options.A: Total loss of blood flow leading to dark, dead tissue at the stoma tip
options.B: Chemical skin burns caused by leaked digestive juices
options.C: Complete blockage of the bowel by tough food particles
options.D: A loop of intestine pushing through a weakened belly wall muscle near the stoma

explanation: Spot on! A parastomal hernia is a weak spot in the muscle around the stoma that lets tummy contents bulge out. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T14#GNS212_U1_T14_h6)

question: Why do we encourage a new colostomy patient to start practicing bag changes early?

options.A: To prove the patient doesn't need emotional counseling anymore
options.B: To make the surgical belly cut heal much faster
options.C: To help the hospital nurses finish their heavy daily chores
options.D: To build self-confidence and lower worry about caring for themselves at home

explanation: You nailed it! Practicing with a nurse nearby helps patients beat their fears and master the skills they need to be independent. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T14#GNS212_U1_T14_h7)

question: What emotional feeling do patients adjusting to a new stoma most commonly experience?

options.B: Immediate excitement to rush back to work

explanation: Spot on. Adjusting to a changed body appearance and worrying about leaks or smells can easily cause stress and emotional upset. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T14#GNS212_U1_T14_h7)
